en: (Give 'im the shrooms?)
Here's yer stuff to experiment on.
You handed over <Color:8>Toxic Mushroom<Color:Default>.
Fantastic! Hey, who knows? Perhaps you just helped me save some lives!
Here's your payment.
You got <Color:8>Tauriner Maximum<Color:Default>.
Sure. Go do yer research. Many people countin' on ya.
Gimme a bit more time.
Ohmigosh, ohmigosh! This is my last chance!
Oh, hey! Aren't you the guy staying with Okudera-san? Can you do me a favor? Please, it's a do-or-die situation!
Uh, settle down there.
I can't! Not if I don't want to die alone! I'm getting on in my years... I need to find a man and get settled! My parents bug me about it every day!
Ugh, but for some reason or another, nobody has ever worked out. Now here I am, a farmer still waiting for her harvest.
And the pressure's really on me now... A relative arranged a meeting with a hot prospect. If I can't land this one, I'm done.
Done, I tell you! And it's just my luck that this blind date is happening during winter... when my skin is always like a scrub brush! I can't even show it to anyone!
Bear fat always worked wonders on my dry skin. Please, you're a hunter. Would you bring me some? Please? Please?
Look, it's against my conscience to kill a bear just for some lotion.
But, if I kill one outta defense or for food, I'll collect the fat for ya.
You will? Thank you! Please don't forget!
"Get Some Bear Fat" was added to the list of missions.
*gasp* It's you! Did you get the bear fat?
(Give 'er the bear fat?)
Here. This what you wanted?
You handed over <Color:8>Bear Fat<Color:Default>.
Ooh, yes! Thank you! I'm one step closer to blessed matrimony!
Heh, just remember chemistry matters more. But good luck.
Oh, and this is my token of thanks. You should get married too, before it's too late for you!
You got <Color:8>Block of Brass<Color:Default>.
Okay, bye!
Not yet. Gimme a little more time.
Aw man, I'm doomed! Doomed!
What's goin' on?
Uh, who are you, big guy?
I'm a guy learnin' how to hunt from people in the village. Sure don't seem like you're from here. What brings ya?
Uh, well actually, I came to hunt something myself... A bear.
And yet you ain't dressed for huntin'. So what's yer story?
Ugh, settle in, man. See, I work part-time at a ramen shop in Tsukimino, and one day, I was making this delivery...
And when I got there, the fucking place was a yakuza office!
Yeah? What happened?
I freaked out when I realized where I was.

I frigging dropped the ramen all over a super expensive
bearskin rug on the floor!!!
And to make things worse, it was an extra-extra-oily, extra-extra-garlicky order!
A what?
Extra-extra-oily, extra-extra-garlicky! The greasiest, smelliest ramen we offer! There wasn't a chance in hell of saving the rug!
Then they looked at me, real stonefaced... It was scary, man! And they said I was gonna replace that rug.
And that's why you're here.
Well, I'm only a part-timer! How am I supposed to afford a swanky item like that? My only way out of this is to shoot the bear myself.
That's crazy talk. It's more likely the bear will end up with <Italic>yer</Italic> skin.

Well, you said you were learning how to hunt. Could you
do it for me? I'll give you what I can as payment...
I ain't willin' to kill a bear just for its skin. But if I happen to kill it for somethin' else, like for meat or defense, I'll take the skin for ya.
That would kick ass! Thanks, dude!
"Get a Bear Skin" was added to the list of missions.
Heyyy, you get the bear skin yet?
(Give it to 'im?)
Will this do?
You handed over <Color:8>Bear Skin<Color:Default>.
Oh, wow! This is even nicer than the rug I ruined! This'll get me square with the yakuza, for sure. I mean, you just saved my frigging life!
Take this! You deserve it!
You got <Color:8>Magnetized Metal<Color:Default>.
So glad I met you, dude! You're the man!
Don't be botherin' me 'bout it. I'll get one when I get one.
I gotcha... But just remember, I'm counting on you, man!
You're that guy living at Okudera's now, aren't you?
Yeah. And you are?
You don't know? Always easy to spot an amateur.
I'm Gonsuke the Trapmaster.
Gonsuke the Trapmaster?
That's my name, don't wear it out! Yeah, I've been trapping in this village for thirty years.
But you, you shoo away one measly bear and now you're strutting around like a hero. Don't get cocky over a fluke, man.
Don't see how I'm cocky, but hey, no problem. You bein' the veteran is fine with me.
Heh. That's right, amateurs ought to show respect. If you see me out there, take some notes. I can teach you all you need about trapping.
"Trapper's Pride" was added to the list of missions.
What're ya doin'?
Oh! Um, nothing! Taking a breather! Everything is just fine.
Ya say that, but...
Are ya caught in yer own trap?
Of course not! This is, um... It's an inspection! I'm testing this trap on myself to make sure it works.
Yep, it's⑬argh!⑬digging in, exactly as it should! Approved! This trap is approved! ...Ow.
Hurts, huh?
Look, an amateur like you couldn't begin to understand the mimetic philosophy of a true hunter. Leave me alone!
Ya sure that's what ya want?
Um... yeah! Get lost!
Well, okay...
Ow! Excellent! No defects at all! This trap will catch any animal just wonderfully... ARGH!!!  I'm so glad that today's inspections are going so well!
Owww, it huuurts...
Hey, you! I can't believe you actually listened to me and left me like this!
No more. Please help me. It hurts like hell. You are the master! Help me, Your Highness! Have mercy.
(Wow... the loudest egos are the feeblest.)
Okay, hold on. Don't squirm.
This trap's pretty much busted. The spring's all loose.
Look at it. You coulda got this off by yerself.
Really? Uh, that's right!
Haha, I was testing you this whole time!
Yup. It's part of any beginner hunter's education. You have to know how to get human beings out of traps.
...We really doin' this again?
Oh, fine, I admit it. You saved me. I'm humiliated... but grateful.
Uh, glad to hear it. Can ya make it home by yerself?
Oh yes, definitely! I'm a tough old hunter, you know...
(I could just keep movin'.)
Hey, wait! Where do you think you're going? Ever heard of lending a helping hand!?
Hey, Saejima-san.
You saved Gonsuke on the mountain, right? He wanted you to have this.
You got <Color:8>Even Goro's Beads<Color:Default>.
Thanks. That fella sure is a... character, isn't he?
Yeah, he's such a blowhard. Goes around talking a big game, but he can barely trap anything. His real trade is fur tanning; he's great as long as the animals are caught by others!
I guess we should thank you for sending him home sniffling. He'll be too embarrassed to show his face in public for a while.
Ah, he's a decent guy. Just too damn vain, even for us prideful villagers.
Hehehe... The winds of fortune are finally blowing my way.
Oh, hey! Thanks for fixing that problem of mine.
Ya sure got a bounce in yer step. How'd that antler work out for ya?
Hehehe, best to leave that to your imagination. But listen, have you heard the rumors about a snowman? Like, the abominable kind.
An abominable snowman? That's silly.
Sure, most people think that, but you never know! There's always a chance, right?
Just think about it. If I caught one, I'd be famous! I'd be all over the news, and the ladies would certainly come running...
What are ya, twelve? Go spend some quality time with yer wife.
Ha! You're just trying to discourage me so you can steal all the glory. Nice try, buddy!
(Seems like too much blood has left his head and gone somewhere else...)
"Chase the Snowman" was added to the list of missions.
Hey, bud. Ya want in on a game? First ya need 25,000 points worth of mahjong sticks. You can buy 'em at the front desk.
Yo, bud. Wanna play? We've got a chair sittin' empty waitin' for a butt.
Great! Sit your butt down and we'll get started.
Bummer. Well, if ya change your mind, you know where to find us.
Hey, bud. You wanna play after all? You'll need at least 25,000 points, so get 'em at the front desk.
Yo, wanna play mahjong with us? Not to brag, but we're pretty tough.
Good answer! Let's not waste time here.
Not up for it? Well, lemme know when you are.
What, ya gotta be somewhere? Well, it's been fun. Lookin' forward to next time.
Man, that was a blast. Gotta do that again sometime.
Hey, bud. Wanna play with us? First ya need 25,000 points worth of mahjong sticks. Get 'em at the front desk.
Yo, bud, tired of standin'? Sit down and play a game with us.
All right! Let's go.
That's too bad. You know who to talk to if you change your line of thinkin'.
Yo, wanna play with us? To be honest, we're kinda decent.
Wasn't that fun? Gotta do that again.
Ya wanna play? There's a seat waitin' for ya.
No, huh? Well, if you get to thinkin' otherwise, here we are.
Hey, you lookin' for a game after all? Gotta get yourself 25,000 points in mahjong sticks at the front desk first.
Yo, lookin' for a game? We're all regulars here. We can give ya a good game.
Hm? Well, imagine seein' ya here. Don't tell me you don't remember me.
I'm the Naniwasienne. Chiaki Takachiho?
That's the name of the woman who's gonna strip ya naked of your assets. Heh. Don't you forget it.
Each participant posts a winner-take-all stake of 100,000 points in addition to the 25,000 needed to play, for a total of 125,000 points.

Rules are set at the start of the match, choosing either a Quarter or a Half Game. At the end of play, the top player wins the entire pot of 400,000 points. If you quit the game, you forfeit your 100,000-point stake.
So, will ya pony up the 100,000 points and play with me?
Good. That's the spirit.
Here. Your 100,000-point stake goes in the pot.
Let's get this party started.
Hey, wait a sec. Ya can't play without your stake. Wanna buy 100,000 points worth of mahjong sticks now?
Sure. I'll buy the 100,000 points.
Good. Your stake's goin' straight into the pot.
Wait a sec. You don't have enough to buy in, do ya? Scrape enough mahjong sticks together first.
Sweetie, that's likely the smartest decision you'll make today. But if ya ever want some stupid thrills, I'm your gal.
Hey there. Lookin' for some high-stakes mahjong?
Ya crushed me... Looks like I've still got some stuff to learn.
There's your pot. All 400,000 points.
Mahjong that thrillin's a rare thing. We gotta do this again sometime.
Thanks for the good time, sweetie. Worth yer 100,000-point stake, right? Say bye to it.
Still, you're a fun boy to play with. If you're lookin' for more thrills, think of this gal. I'm yours anytime.
What, you're leavin' in the middle of things? You can kiss yer 100,000-point stake goodbye. We'll split it up.
Hey, bud, don't I know ya? From Riichi Tower, right? Fancy sittin' down for some mahjong with us? We're a man short.
Good answer! Let's get started.
Hold it, you ain't got no mahjong sticks. Wanna buy 25,000 points worth so you can play?
You're the man. Let's start.
No, huh? Well, if you get to thinkin' otherwise, I'll be right here.
Yo, how 'bout you join us for some mahjong?
Good answer! Let's get goin', then.
You're the man. Let's do this.
What, you gotta run? Well, that was fun. Come play again sometime!
Man, that was a blast. Gotta do that again sometime!
Good answer! Let's get started, then.
Hold it. Got no mahjong sticks? How about I sell ya 25,000 points worth so you can play?
No, huh? Well, if you get to thinkin' otherwise, we'll be right here.
You. Hold on a sec.
Huh? Who're you?
Please, that any way to treat a lady? Are you sayin' you play mahjong around here and you don't recognize the Naniwasienne?
The nani... what?
Taken by my appearance, huh? Had to start dressin' like this when I started playin' mahjong. A girl gets a lot of unwanted attention in your rougher mahjong parlors.
'Course nowadays, I'm well-known around these parts, so there ain't no man fool enough to mess with me.
I can get that. What do you want from me, though?
Makes sense. So what can I do for you?
Wanna play mahjong with a bit more edge? You're gettin' bored with the nickel-and-dime game, aren't ya?
If you want, I can arrange high-stakes matches. You can come out rich... or leave with the shirt on yer back and not much more.
I'm Chiaki Takachiho. Like I said before, though, people call me the Naniwasienne.
Anytime's a good time for mahjong, okay? If you're willin' to risk everythin' for a spot of fun, look me up.
